subject: Service-level metrics and dispute process — post-call recap
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Amanda Taylor <amanda.taylor@olivehealth.com>
Cc: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay.reddy@olivehealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@olivehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Service-level metrics and dispute process — post-call recap

Amanda / Sanjay — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from my side to capture what we agreed and the open items before legal/procurement review. Please flag anything I missed.

Key goals we heard on the call:
- Latency: p95 end-to-end (request received -> first token out) target of 200ms for single-turn queries; streaming sessions require per-chunk TTFB <= 100ms and stable chunk cadence for UX.
- Throughput & concurrency: baseline of 250 req/s sustained with burst to 600 req/s; concurrent streaming sessions target of 120 concurrent sessions.
- Measurement: rolling 30-day window for SLO calculation; reporting via daily dashboard + monthly SLA report.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (pre-notified 24h), region outages, customer-triggered rate spikes outside agreed request model, and model fallback events (we will capture and label these).
- Remedies: proposed credit schedule was discussed loosely (we will provide formal contract language).

Open questions we committed to answer:
1) Exact measurement definition for streaming (per-chunk vs full session).
2) How we handle cold-starts and autoscaling-related latency blips.
3) Proposed reporting cadence and log access (example S3 location + retention).
4) Draft remedial language for credits, measurement windows, and dispute process.

Quick proposal for next steps: 
- We (Redwood) will send a measurement spec + suggested contract wording by EOD tomorrow for review.
- Olive to provide example QPS/shape (peak hours, typical session lengths) so we can validate capacity plan.
- Procurement to confirm any mandatory contract clauses (security/compliance) that affect remedy mechanics.

Thanks — I'll drop the spec as an attachment and follow up with a short acceptance-test proposal for the pilot.

—
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
E: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai | M: (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Service-level metrics and dispute process — post-call recap

Thanks, Evelyn — good summary. A couple of clarifying items before we get into legal review: 

1) Streaming measurement: when you say "per-chunk TTFB <= 100ms" do you measure from the moment our client posts the next prompt chunk, or from when the server acknowledges receipt? For UX reasons we measure perceived latency from client send -> first visible byte; want to ensure the contract aligns.

2) Cold starts: if a session experiences a cold start because model instance scale-up was required, do you propose this as an exclusion or bucket it as a quantifiable event (e.g., excluded for first 5 minutes after autoscale)? We need clarity for our incident postmortems.

3) Remedies: procurement will want a clear credit table and an escalation timeline (e.g., customer raises dispute -> Redwood responds within 5 business days -> remediation plan within 15 business days). Can you include a suggested dispute timeline?

Also copying procurement — procurement, please confirm any non-negotiable SLA clauses on your side.

—Amanda
Amanda Taylor
Director, Product — Olive Health
amanda.taylor@olivehealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Amanda Taylor <amanda.taylor@olivehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@olivehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service-level metrics and dispute process — post-call recap

Amanda / team — looping in legal/contract perspective and a proposed set of measurable contract bullets. High-level notes:

- Measurement definitions (suggested contract wording):
  * "End-to-end latency (ms)" = elapsed time between Redwood ingress timestamp (request received at edge) and time of first byte delivered to customer client.
  * "Streaming chunk latency (ms)" = elapsed time between chunk receive timestamp and first token emitted for that chunk. SLOs expressed as p50/p95/p99 over the rolling window.
  * "Throughput (req/s)" = number of accepted requests per second at Redwood ingress; concurrency = number of active token-generating sessions.

- Exclusions (contract): scheduled maintenance (>=24h notice), force majeure, region-level cloud provider incidents, customer-generated bursts exceeding agreed traffic profile, and authenticated API misuse causing malformed payloads.

- Cold-start handling: propose limited exclusion for scale-up events that exceed predicted capacity if they occur fewer than X times per month; otherwise they count toward SLO. We will supply scaling logs labeled for review.

- Remedies (sample table):
  * Monthly p95 > 200ms but <= 300ms: 5% service credit (monthly invoice)
  * Monthly p95 > 300ms but <= 500ms: 10% credit
  * Monthly p95 > 500ms: 25% credit + joint remediation plan within 10 business days
  * Streaming chunk p95 breach: 5% credit per breach window; repeated breaches trigger escalation.

- Dispute process (proposed):
  1) Customer raises dispute via hubspot ticket + email to eng-ops@redwood.ai.
  2) Redwood acknowledges within 2 business days, provides initial logs and measurement excerpt within 5 business days.
  3) Parties agree on joint measurement sample or appoint an independent measurement snapshot process within 10 business days.

I'll attach a short draft clause that legal can adapt. Evelyn — happy to have Marissa drive the SLO wording into a redline.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
Attachment: contractual_slo_draft.txt

This is helpful. Procurement here — two items we need spelled out for internal approval: 
1) Acceptance criteria for pilot: what exact tests do we run (soak, 1-hour ramp to peak, 30-minute sustained streaming sample) and what pass/fail thresholds do we use? We need these to sign off the pilot.
2) Logs and evidence: we need read-only access to the raw measurement export (timestamped ingress, trunk IDs, latency measurements) for the pilot duration. Please confirm S3 path and retention policy; we will need 90-day retention.

Also, please confirm the dispute timeline: our legal team expects Redwood to provide initial measurement export within 3 business days of a dispute and an engineering root-cause analysis within 10 business days. The timelines are negotiable but would like them in the draft.

Thanks — Procurement (on behalf of Olive Health)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

Amanda / Procurement / Ben — thanks all for the quick responses. Per commitments below, attached is the draft measurement_specification_v1.pdf and a short ops_runbook_stub.txt (attachment stubs). Summary of agreed items and next steps below — please review and confirm by end of week so legal can start redlining.

Agreed (draft) items:
- Measurement: use Redwood ingress timestamps for end-to-end p50/p95/p99 calculations; streaming chunk latency measured per-chunk with session correlation ID. Rolling window = 30 days for monthly SLA calculation.
- Pilot acceptance tests (suggested):
  * Soak: 4-hour run at 80% target throughput (200 req/s) with p95 < 220ms allowed.
  * Ramp: 1-hour linear ramp to 600 req/s peak with sustained 10-minute intervals at peak.
  * Streaming sample: 30-minute streaming test with 120 concurrent sessions and per-chunk p95 < 120ms.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (24h notice), documented cloud provider incidents, known misuse. Cold-starts: exclude only for scale-up events fewer than 3/month; otherwise, count toward SLO.
- Remedies & dispute timeline (proposal):
  * Redwood acknowledges disputes within 2 business days and provides measurement export within 3 business days.
  * RCA and remediation plan within 10 business days for confirmed breaches.
  * Credit table as proposed by Ben above.

Deliverables (who/when):
- Redwood to share final spec (measurement_specification_v1.pdf) and ops runbook stub — DONE (attached).
- Olive to share production traffic shape + example payloads by 2026-09-13. (Owner: Amanda / Sanjay)
- Legal redlines: Procurement/legal to send first redline by 2026-09-17. (Owner: Procurement)
- Pilot scheduling: schedule 2-week pilot window once traffic shape is received. (Owner: Evelyn)

If that matches your expectations, I'll drop the S3 export path for read-only access and create the HubSpot ticket (HS-4831) so disputes are tracked automatically.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

—
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
